verifications.claim: Aerojet Rocketdyne is an L3Harris company.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Aerojet Rocketdyne, an L3Harris Technologies Company
verifications.reasoning: Directly states Aerojet Rocketdyne as an L3Harris Technologies Company in the list of SLS prime contractors.

verifications.claim: Lockheed Martin builds the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Orion spacecraft built by Lockheed Martin (R1); Orion crew capsule – built by Lockheed Martin (R2); Lockheed Martin is the lead contractor for the design, development testing, and production of the Orion spacecraft (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state Lockheed Martin builds or is the prime contractor for Orion.

verifications.claim: Boeing produces the 212-foot core stage for the Artemis missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 212-foot core stage propelled by four engines (R2); Boeing will produce SLS core stages (R4); Boeing is responsible for building the core stage (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Boeing builds the core stage and specify its height as 212 feet.

verifications.claim: The 212-foot core stage houses the main engines and flight systems.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: 212-foot core stage propelled by four engines powered by a mix of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen (R2); SLS core stage ... producing more than 2 million pounds of thrust (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Confirms 212-foot core stage has main engines (RS-25), but 'flight systems' is broader and not explicitly detailed.

verifications.claim: Northrop Grumman manufactures the twin five-segment solid rocket boosters for the Artemis missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: two 177-feet-tall solid rocket boosters ... built by Boeing and Northrop Grumman (R2); Northrop Grumman manufactures the five-segment solid rocket boosters (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm Northrop Grumman builds the five-segment solid rocket boosters for SLS/Artemis.

verifications.claim: The twin five-segment solid rocket boosters provide 75% of the thrust at launch.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: two 177-feet-tall solid rocket boosters mounted to the sides providing the bulk of the thrust
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe boosters providing 'the bulk' of thrust (implying majority like 75%), but no exact percentage given.

verifications.claim: Aerojet Rocketdyne supplies the RS-25 engines for the Artemis missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: RS-25 engines (R1); Aerojet Rocketdyne is building the engines ... RS-25 engine (R7); four RS-25D engines (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources link Aerojet Rocketdyne to RS-25 engines used in SLS core stage for Artemis.

verifications.claim: Aerojet Rocketdyne supplies other propulsion systems for the Artemis missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Aerojet Rocketdyne provides eight auxiliary engines and 12 reaction control thrusters for the Orion crew module, as well as the jettison motor for the LAS
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly lists additional propulsion systems beyond RS-25 engines supplied by Aerojet Rocketdyne for Orion/Artemis.

verifications.claim: Airbus builds the European Service Module (ESM) for the Orion capsule for the European Space Agency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: ESM: Airbus (R9); Orion’s European Service Module, which is built by its main contractor, Airbus (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state Airbus builds the ESM for ESA under Orion program.

verifications.claim: United Launch Alliance (ULA) developed the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: SLS built by Boeing and United Launch Alliance (R1); interim cryogenic propulsion stage, is built by United Launch Alliance (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm ULA builds/develops the ICPS upper stage for SLS.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew's journey in space has begun.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: NASA's Artemis II mission will send four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon (R2, dated 2026 pre-launch); NASA's Orion spacecraft ... marking the completion of the historic Artemis II mission. During its nearly 10-day journey (R8, post-mission)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe Artemis II as launched and completed, confirming the crew's journey began.

verifications.claim: NASA manages the Space Launch System (SLS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) (R1); NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) Program manager (R4); NASA’s prime contractors for SLS (R5)
verifications.reasoning: All sources attribute SLS management and program oversight to NASA.

verifications.claim: Space Launch System (SLS) components are manufactured across the U.S. and in Europe.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: thousands of people work together—across states, countries, and even continents (R1); more than 2,700 suppliers across 47 states ... Airbus built the arrays in the Netherlands (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources note manufacturing across US states and international involvement (e.g., Europe via Airbus for related components), but primarily US for core SLS parts.
